claim: Two laboratory lineages of C. elegans, N2 and LSJ2, descended from a single hermaphrodite isolated in 1951.
source: These two lineages split from genetically identical populations between 1957 and 1958 and evolved in two very different laboratory environments – N2 grew on agar plates seeded with E. coli bacteria and LSJ2 in liquid cultures containing liver and soy peptone extracts (McGrath et al., 2009; McGrath et al., 2011; Sterken et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to previous publications.

claim: The N2 and LSJ2 lineages split between 1957 and 1958.
source: These two lineages split from genetically identical populations between 1957 and 1958 and evolved in two very different laboratory environments – N2 grew on agar plates seeded with E. coli bacteria and LSJ2 in liquid cultures containing liver and soy peptone extracts (McGrath et al., 2009; McGrath et al., 2011; Sterken et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: N2 grew on agar plates seeded with E. coli bacteria.
source: These two lineages split from genetically identical populations between 1957 and 1958 and evolved in two very different laboratory environments – N2 grew on agar plates seeded with E. coli bacteria and LSJ2 in liquid cultures containing liver and soy peptone extracts (McGrath et al., 2009; McGrath et al., 2011; Sterken et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: LSJ2 grew in liquid cultures containing liver and soy peptone extracts.
source: These two lineages split from genetically identical populations between 1957 and 1958 and evolved in two very different laboratory environments – N2 grew on agar plates seeded with E. coli bacteria and LSJ2 in liquid cultures containing liver and soy peptone extracts (McGrath et al., 2009; McGrath et al., 2011; Sterken et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: Approximately 300-2000 generations passed before permanent means of cryopreservation were developed.
source: By the time permanent means of cryopreservation were developed, approximately 300–2000 generations had passed, and ~ 300 new mutations arose and fixed in one of the two lineages (McGrath et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Approximately 300 new mutations arose and fixed in one of the two lineages.
source: By the time permanent means of cryopreservation were developed, approximately 300–2000 generations had passed, and ~ 300 new mutations arose and fixed in one of the two lineages (McGrath et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Substantial divergence has occurred between N2 and LSJ2 strains in terms of phenotype and fitness.
source: Despite their genetic similarity, substantial divergence has occurred between these strains in terms of phenotype and fitness, including a large number of developmental, behavioral, and reproductive traits.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Five de novo, causal genetic variants have been identified in either the N2 or LSJ2 lineage.
source: To date, five de novo, causal genetic variants have been identified in either the N2 or LSJ2 lineage (de Bono and Bargmann, 1998; McGrath et al., 2009; Persson et al., 2009; McGrath et al., 2011; Duveau and Félix, 2012; Large et al., 2016; Large et al., 2017; Zhao et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by multiple citations.

claim: nurf-1 encodes an ortholog of BPTF, a large (>300 kD) multidomain subunit of the NURF chromatin remodeling complex.
source: nurf-1 encodes an ortholog of BPTF, a large (>300 kD) multidomain subunit of the NURF chromatin remodeling complex.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: In C. elegans, nurf-1 has split into two, largely non-overlapping isoforms (NURF-1.D and NURF-1.B) that share only two of 26 exons.
source: Using CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing and transgenic rescue, we demonstrate that in C. elegans, nurf-1 has split into two, largely non-overlapping isoforms (NURF-1.D and NURF-1.B, which we call Yin and Yang, respectively) that share only two of 26 exons.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by experimental methods described.

claim: Both NURF-1.D and NURF-1.B isoforms are essential for normal gametogenesis.
source: Both isoforms are essential for normal gametogenesis but have opposite effects on male/female gamete differentiation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: NURF-1.D and NURF-1.B isoforms have opposite effects on male/female gamete differentiation.
source: Both isoforms are essential for normal gametogenesis but have opposite effects on male/female gamete differentiation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Reproduction in hermaphrodites requires a balance of the opposing Yin and Yang isoforms.
source: Reproduction in hermaphrodites, which involves production of both sperm and oocytes, requires a balance of these opposing Yin and Yang isoforms.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: In a related clade of Caenorhabditis nematodes, the shared exons have duplicated, resulting in the split of the Yin and Yang isoforms into separate genes.
source: In a related clade of Caenorhabditis nematodes, the shared exons have duplicated, resulting in the split of the Yin and Yang isoforms into separate genes, each containing approximately 200 amino acids of duplicated sequence that has undergone accelerated protein evolution following the duplication.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The duplicated sequence has undergone accelerated protein evolution following the duplication.
source: In a related clade of Caenorhabditis nematodes, the shared exons have duplicated, resulting in the split of the Yin and Yang isoforms into separate genes, each containing approximately 200 amino acids of duplicated sequence that has undergone accelerated protein evolution following the duplication.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Associated with the duplication event is the loss of two additional nurf-1 transcripts, including the long-form transcript and a newly identified, highly expressed transcript encoded by the duplicated exons.
source: Associated with this duplication event is the loss of two additional nurf-1 transcripts, including the long-form transcript and a newly identified, highly expressed transcript encoded by the duplicated exons.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The lost transcripts are non-functional side products necessary to transcribe the Yin and Yang transcripts in the same cells.
source: We propose these lost transcripts are non-functional side products necessary to transcribe the Yin and Yang transcripts in the same cells.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a proposal by the authors.

claim: Gene sharing, through the production of multiple isoforms, can precede the creation of new, independent genes.
source: Our work demonstrates how gene sharing, through the production of multiple isoforms, can precede the creation of new, independent genes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the work.

claim: An N2-derived variant in the second intron of nurf-1 increases fitness and brood size in laboratory conditions.
source: An N2-derived variant in the second intron of nurf-1 increases fitness and brood size in laboratory conditions
evidence: This is a section heading that summarizes experimental findings.

claim: The LSJ2 allele of nurf-1 contains a 60 bp deletion in the 3' end of the coding region of the gene.
source: The LSJ2 allele of nurf-1 contains a 60 bp deletion in the 3' end of the coding region of the gene, overlapping the stop codon and probably resulting in the translation of parts of the 3' UTR.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The N2 allele of nurf-1 contains an SNV that converts an A to a T in a homopolymer run of Ts in the 2nd intron.
source: The N2 allele of nurf-1 contains an SNV that converts an A to a T in a homopolymer run of Ts in the 2nd intron (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to Figure 1B.

claim: The LSJ2-derived deletion accounted for a large portion of the trait variance in reproductive rate explained by the QTL.
source: Using CRISPR-Cas9-based genome editing, we previously demonstrated that the LSJ2-derived deletion accounted for a large portion of the trait variance in reproductive rate explained by the QTL.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and refers to previous work.

claim: The NIL(nurf-1,LSJ2>N2*) strain was quantitatively and significantly less fit than the ARL(del,LSJ2>N2*) strain.
source: However, the NIL(nurf-1,LSJ2>N2*) was quantitatively and significantly less fit than the ARL(del,LSJ2>N2*) strain, suggesting additional genetic variant(s) in the NIL(nurf-1,LSJ2>N2*) strain further reduced its fitness.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2*) strain was significantly less fit than the N2 strain.
source: The ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2*) strain was significantly less fit than the N2 strain at a level similar to the difference between the NIL(nurf-1,LSJ2>N2*) and ARL(del,LSJ2>N2) strains (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to Figure 1D.

claim: Beneficial alleles of nurf-1 arose in both laboratory lineages.
source: These results indicate that beneficial alleles of nurf-1 arose in both laboratory lineages - the 60 bp deletion makes LSJ2 animals more fit in liquid, axenic media (Large et al., 2016), and the intron SNV makes N2 animals more fit on agar plates seeded with bacteria.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: The ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2) strain produced approximately 30 fewer offspring than N2.
source: When we compared the total fecundity produced by the N2 and ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2) strains, we found a significant difference, with the ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2) strain producing ~ 30 fewer offspring than N2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to Figure 1E.

claim: A large number of genes are differentially expressed between N2 and ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2) strains but only during the 52 hr timepoint (3384 genes vs. 25 genes).
source: Interestingly, a large number of genes are differentially expressed between the two strains but only during the 52 hr timepoint (3384 genes vs. 25 genes) (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures and supplementary files.

claim: Gene ontology analysis suggests that cuticle development and innate immune responses are regulated by nurf-1.
source: Gene ontology analysis suggests that cuticle development and innate immune responses are regulated by nurf-1 (Supplementary file 2) consistent with the role of its orthologs in regulating immunity and melanocyte proliferation in Drosophila and humans (Kwon et al., 2008; Landry et al., 2011; Koludrovic et al., 2015; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: Previous cDNA analysis of nurf-1 identified four unique transcripts encoding four unique isoforms.
source: Previous cDNA analysis of nurf-1 identified four unique transcripts encoding four unique isoforms (Andersen et al., 2006), two of which have been shown to affect different phenotypes (summarized in Table 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Five major transcripts of nurf-1 were identified: nurf-1.a, nurf-1.b, nurf-1.d, nurf-1.f, and nurf-1.q.
source: We identified five major transcripts (Figure 2A) - three previously isolated (nurf-1.b, nurf-1.d, and nurf-1.f) but also two newly identified (nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q) (mapping of transcript names used in Andersen et al. are listed in Table 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to Figure 2A.

claim: nurf-1.a encodes a full-length 2197 amino acid isoform analogous to the primary isoform of BPTF in humans and NURF301 in Drosophila.
source: nurf-1.a encodes a full-length 2197 amino acid isoform analogous to the primary isoform of BPTF in humans and NURF301 in Drosophila (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to Figure 1C.

claim: The nurf-1.q transcript is predicted to produce a 243 amino acid unstructured protein.
source: The nurf-1.q transcript is predicted to produce a 243 amino acid unstructured protein.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The newly described nurf-1.q transcript was the most highly expressed followed by the nurf-1.b transcript.
source: Surprisingly, the newly described nurf-1.q transcript was the most highly expressed followed by the nurf-1.b transcript, and the nurf-1.a, nurf-1.d and nurf-1.f were expressed at similar lower levels.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Immunoblot analysis supported the expression of the B, D, and F isoforms, but not the A or Q isoforms.
source: Immunoblot analysis supported the expression of the B, D, and F isoforms, but not the A or Q isoforms (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to Figure 2D.

claim: Analysis of all five nurf-1 transcript levels did not reveal any significant expression differences between N2 and ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2) strains.
source: However, analysis of all five nurf-1 transcript levels, using the previously described RNA-seq data on the N2 and ARL(intron,LSJ2>N2) strains, did not reveal any significant expression differences (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: A number of additional bands were observed between 150–250 kD in western blots on human cancer cell lines.
source: Interestingly, besides a band matching the expected size of the canonical full-length isoform, a number of additional bands were observed between 150–250 kD (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: Mass-spectrometry confirmed the presence of multiple BPTF peptides in the bands detected by western blotting.
source: Using mass-spectrometry, we confirmed the presence of multiple BPTF peptides in the bands detected by western blotting (Figure 2—figure supplement 4), consistent with one or more of these bands representing novel BPTF isoforms.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: The full-length version of BPTF is the most highly expressed isoform in human cancer cells.
source: Despite the presence of these additional bands, the full-length version of BPTF is the most highly expressed isoform (Figure 2—figure supplement 4D), consistent with its importance in mammalian species.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: The n4293 allele deletes the first exon and predicted transcriptional start site of the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.b transcripts.
source: The n4293 allele deletes the first exon and predicted transcriptional start site of the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.b transcripts.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The n4295 allele deletes three exons of the nurf-1.a, nurf-1.d, and nurf.1.f transcripts that encode a C-terminal PHD domain.
source: The n4295 allele deletes three exons of the nurf-1.a, nurf-1.d, and nurf.1.f transcripts that encode a C-terminal PHD domain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) necessary for human BPTF function.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: Engineering stop codons in the first, second, and 7th exons greatly reduced fecundity, resulting in either sterility, or a mortal germline phenotype.
source: As expected, engineering stop codons in the first, second, and 7th exons greatly reduced fecundity, resulting in either sterility, or a mortal germline phenotype, initially reducing total brood size of animals, before eventually causing complete sterility after around three-to-five generations of homozygosity (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures.

claim: Engineering stop codons in the 18th and 19th exons also caused a mortal germline phenotype.
source: Unexpectedly, engineering stop codons in the 18th and 19th exons also caused a mortal germline phenotype (kah96 and kah99) (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: The kah68 allele phenocopies the n4295 allele and not the kah96 and kah99 animals.
source: However, the kah68 allele, which contains a stop codon within the n4295 deleted region, phenocopies the n4295 allele and not the kah96 and kah99 animals (Figure 3B and C, and Figure 3—figure supplement 2)).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures.

claim: The double mutant containing both the n4295 allele and the 18th exon stop allele phenocopied the kah96 single mutant.
source: However, we could exclude this possibility as the double mutant containing both the n4295 allele and the 18th exon stop allele phenocopied the kah96 single mutant (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: Specific loss of the F isoform by the 23rd exon stop allele (kah11) did not affect the phenotype of animals.
source: Additionally, specific loss of the F isoform by the 23rd exon stop allele (kah11) did not affect the phenotype of animals (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures.

claim: The ability of NURF-1 to bind modified histones is not required for its function.
source: Our data suggest that, unlike human BPTF, the ability of NURF-1 to bind modified histones is not required for its function.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The D isoform is required for reproduction and wild-type growth rate.
source: The most parsimonious explanation of our data is that either the A or D isoform is essential for reproduction in C. elegans. Compound heterozygote tests allowed us to distinguish between these possibilities, indicating that the D isoform is required for reproduction and wild-type growth rate, and the A isoform is dispensable for reproduction and development (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: The A isoform is dispensable for reproduction and development.
source: The most parsimonious explanation of our data is that either the A or D isoform is essential for reproduction in C. elegans. Compound heterozygote tests allowed us to distinguish between these possibilities, indicating that the D isoform is required for reproduction and wild-type growth rate, and the A isoform is dispensable for reproduction and development (Figure 4).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: kah106/kah96 compound heterozygotes were indistinguishable from wild-type.
source: However, these animals were indistinguishable from wild-type, suggesting that the full-length A isoform is not essential (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: kah93/kah96 compound heterozygotes were essentially sterile.
source: Finally, we analyzed kah93/kah96 compound heterozygotes. These animals are predicted to encode zero wild-type copies of the D isoform, one wild-type copy of the B isoform, and zero wild-type copies of the A isoform. These animals were essentially sterile.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Both the B and the D isoform are both essential for reproduction.
source: Taken together, we conclude that the B and the D isoform are both essential for reproduction.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a conclusion.

claim: A transgenic strain containing an integrated construct driving a nurf-1.d cDNA from its endogenous promoter could fully rescue the fecundity phenotype of the kah96 allele.
source: This transgene could fully rescue the fecundity phenotype of the kah96 allele and partially rescue the fecundity phenotype of the kah93 allele (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: The F isoform is involved in the heat shock response.
source: Although the F isoform does not seem to have an effect in normally developing animals, it is involved in the heat shock response.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The nurf-1.f transcript was specifically upregulated in response to heat shock.
source: By analyzing RNA-seq reads from these two papers, we found that the nurf-1.f transcript was specifically upregulated in both datasets, with increased coverage of the 23rd exon as well as the 24th through 28th exons (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figure supplements.

claim: The increased transcription of the nurf-1.f transcript also increased NURF-1.F protein abundance.
source: We confirmed that the increased transcription of the nurf-1.f transcript also increased NURF-1.F protein abundance (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figure supplements.

claim: The F isoform plays a modulatory role in determining the long-term transcriptional response to heat shock.
source: We conclude that the F isoform is specifically up-regulated by heat shock and plays a modulatory role in determining the long-term transcriptional response to heat shock.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a conclusion.

claim: The number of sperm produced by kah106 animals was greatly reduced, resulting in the production of only approximately 60 sperm.
source: Compared with N2 animals, which create ~ 300 sperm per animal, the number of sperm produced by kah106 animals was greatly reduced, resulting in the production of only approximately 60 sperm (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: kah106 animals produced a normal number of oocytes.
source: These animals produced a normal number of oocytes, indicating that spermatogenesis seemed to be affected specifically (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: Hermaphrodites that lack the NURF-1.B isoform spend less time in spermatogenesis before transitioning to oogenesis.
source: We interpret these data as evidence that hermaphrodites that lack the NURF-1.B isoform spend less time in spermatogenesis before transitioning to oogenesis.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: kah96 mutants produced approximately 500 sperm and almost no oocytes.
source: We next tested kah96 mutants which lack the D isoform. These animals produced approximately 500 sperm and almost no oocytes (Figure 5C-E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures.

claim: Hermaphrodites that lack the D isoform are unable to transition from spermatogenesis to oogenesis.
source: We interpret these data as evidence that hermaphrodites that lack the D isoform are unable to transition from spermatogenesis to oogenesis.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: kah93 mutants showed an intermediate phenotype, with normal number of sperm but reduced number of oocytes.
source: Finally, we performed similar experiments on kah93 mutants, which lack the D isoform and have a truncated B isoform. These animals showed an intermediate phenotype, with normal number of sperm but reduced number of oocytes (Figure 5D and E).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures.

claim: Both the N2 and LSJ2-derived alleles in nurf-1 regulate the activity of a common molecular target, which is likely to be the NURF complex.
source: The most parsimonious explanation for this observation is that both the N2 and LSJ2-derived alleles in nurf-1 regulate the activity of a common molecular target, which is likely to be the NURF complex.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: In C. briggsae, transcripts matching the nurf-1.b and nurf-1.d no longer shared any exons with each other, suggesting that they were expressed from two separate genes.
source: Interestingly, although transcripts matching the nurf-1.b and nurf-1.d were isolated from this species, they no longer shared any exons with each other, suggesting that they were expressed from two separate genes (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: The shared exons in C. elegans had duplicated in C. briggsae, with one set of each retained in each of the new genes.
source: We compared the gene products using BLAST and found that the shared exons in C. elegans had duplicated in C. briggsae, with one set of each retained in each of the new genes (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: C. briggsae seemed to have lost both the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q transcripts.
source: Unlike C. elegans, C. briggsae seemed to have lost both the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q transcripts.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The exon duplication and separation of nurf-1 into separate genes occurred at the base of a clade containing 11 described species, including C. brenneri and C. tribulationis.
source: Analysis of the nurf-1 gene structure within the context of the Caenorhabditis phylogeny suggested that the exon duplication and separation of nurf-1 into separate genes occurred at the base of a clade containing 11 described species, including C. brenneri and C. tribulationis (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure.

claim: None of the species in the brenneri/tribulationis clade appears to express nurf-1.a or nurf-1.q transcripts.
source: None of these species appears to express nurf-1.a or nurf-1.q transcripts (Figure 6—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figure supplements.

claim: The C. elegans transcript structure is ancestral.
source: These data suggest that the C. elegans transcript structure is ancestral.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the data.

claim: The split of nurf-1 into two distinct genes happened once within the common ancestor of the brenneri/tribulationis clade.
source: The analysis supported the model that the split of nurf-1 into two distinct genes happened once within the common ancestor of the brenneri/tribulationis clade (Figure 6C – additional possible trees shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to figures.

claim: The rate of amino acid substitution in the duplicated region was accelerated in nurf-1–1 relative to nurf-1–2.
source: Interestingly, the rate of amino acid substitution in the duplicated region was accelerated in nurf-1–1 relative to nurf-1–2 (p<0.001; Welch's t-test) suggesting that this region experienced positive selection and/or relaxed selection after this duplication event occurred.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by statistical analysis.

claim: Comparison of the synonymous vs. non-synonymous substitution rate in three closely-related species pairs was consistent with an increase in the rate of protein evolution in the duplicated region following the separation of nurf-1 into independent genes.
source: Comparison of the synonymous vs. non-synonymous substitution rate in three closely-related species pairs was also consistent with an increase in the rate of protein evolution in the duplicated region following the separation of nurf-1 into independent genes (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a table.

claim: nurf-1 is a genetic target for adaptation to the extreme changes in environments associated with laboratory growth.
source: Our work suggests nurf-1 is a genetic target for adaptation to the extreme changes in environments associated with laboratory growth.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a conclusion from the work.

claim: The LSJ2-derived deletion in nurf-1 modified life history tradeoffs to prioritize individual survival over reproduction.
source: The LSJ2-derived deletion in nurf-1 modified life history tradeoffs to prioritize individual survival over reproduction; by shunting energy away from reproduction and growth, they increased their chances of surviving on poor, unnatural food.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The N2 mutation favors reproduction while the LSJ2 mutation favors survival.
source: The N2 mutation favors reproduction while the LSJ2 mutation favors survival.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Genetic alterations in BPTF have been reported in several types of cancer.
source: In humans, genetic alterations in BPTF have been reported in several types of cancer and a role of BPTF in transcriptional regulation by c-MYC has been demonstrated, in agreement with its chromatin-binding function (Richart et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: A role of BPTF in transcriptional regulation by c-MYC has been demonstrated.
source: In humans, genetic alterations in BPTF have been reported in several types of cancer and a role of BPTF in transcriptional regulation by c-MYC has been demonstrated, in agreement with its chromatin-binding function (Richart et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: Multiple BPTF peptides were confirmed in the bands detected by western blotting using mass-spectrometry.
source: Using mass-spectrometry, we confirmed the presence of multiple BPTF peptides in the bands detected by western blotting (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and referenced to a figure supplement.

claim: The separation of the two isoforms into two distinct genes does not signify any important evolutionary change in the function of the two genes under the developmental system drift scenario.
source: Under this scenario, the separation of the two isoforms into two distinct genes does not signify any important evolutionary change in the function of the two genes.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as part of a hypothetical scenario.

claim: Loss of the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q transcripts could have provided a fitness benefit for animals.
source: Loss of these transcripts could have provided a fitness benefit for animals.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a speculation.

claim: The nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q transcripts are non-functional biproducts of molecular conflict between nurf-1.b and nurf-1.d.
source: Intriguingly, these two transcripts match nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q, suggesting these transcripts are non-functional biproducts of molecular conflict between nurf-1.b and nurf-1.d.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a suggestion.

claim: Production of the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q transcripts could come at an energetic cost.
source: Potentially, production of the nurf-1.a and nurf-1.q transcripts could come at an energetic cost.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a speculation.

claim: The nurf-1.q transcript is either not translated or the protein product is rapidly degraded.
source: First, while the nurf-1.q transcript is produced at high levels, we were unable to observe its product in our immunoblots, suggesting that it is either not translated or the protein product is rapidly degraded.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Duplication of the shared exons could facilitate future evolutionary change.
source: Second, duplication of the shared exons could facilitate future evolutionary change.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text as a speculation.

claim: Escape from adaptive conflict is a mechanism by which gene duplication can resolve the situation where a single gene is selected to perform multiple roles.
source: Escape from adaptive conflict is a mechanism by which gene duplication can resolve the situation where a single gene is selected to perform multiple roles (Des Marais and Rausher, 2008).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: The most rapidly evolving portion of the protein is within the 14th and 15th exons.
source: The most rapidly evolving portion of the protein is within the 14th and 15th exons, suggesting positive selection acts on this region of the protein, potentially changing the transcription factors NURF-1 binds to.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: In the clade of nematodes that have duplicated nurf-1, each gene is free to evolve independently.
source: In the clade of nematodes that have duplicated nurf-1, each gene is free to evolve independently.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: In species with duplicated nurf-1, the duplicated region is free to evolve more rapidly.
source: We present evidence that in these species, the duplicated region is free to evolve more rapidly.

claim: BPTF regulates cellular differentiation and homeostasis of specific cell-types and tissues in mammals.
